items.name: 7 coins and 5 paper cups
items.why: The week 1 invariant puzzles are meant to be done with hands, not only in the head.

items.name: A plain envelope and a card for the sealed final motion
items.why: The season's final motion is sealed in week 1 and opened in week 10; it sits on a shelf in between.

items.name: Expedition wall map: poster board, markers, small flag pins
items.why: Twelve waypoints, a flag at each summit, and the two far peaks drawn far off with their dates written in by a grown-up.

items.name: Field journal (blank notebook)
items.why: Holds every sprint's proof pages and puzzle notes across the season, and carries into later seasons.

items.name: Git installed on the laptop
items.why: Save points on the trail: init, commit, and restoring a file from an earlier camp. Free, and local only until week 3.

items.name: Sand timers, 2 minute and 1 minute, and a call bell
items.why: Formal debate needs a referee both sides share; the bell becomes a younger sibling's or a parent's timekeeper job at week 4.

items.name: USACO account (parent-created)
items.why: Submitting past Bronze problems to the real grader from week 2 onward; free, and the account is the parent's.

items.name: Electronics restock: solder, LEDs and battery holders
items.why: Only if their product turns out to be electronic. The Season 2 bench already has the tools, and battery holders are here because no loose coin cell is allowed in a house with a young child.

items.name: Venture seed capital, a loan repaid from revenue
items.why: The shop's materials money for the first production run. The cap is the family's to set and the loan is real, paid back in cash at week 9.

items.name: Storage box or tray
items.why: Keeps the shop's finished production units safe and countable between work sessions.

items.name: AAA batteries, restock
items.why: Keeps the micro:bit's scrolling OPEN sign running fresh for Market Day.

items.name: Market Day kit: cash box, coin float in change, price tag blanks, sign board
items.why: Week 7 dresses the stand and counts the float twice; week 8 sells from it. The float of about 10 comes home after the sale.

items.name: Basic calculator
items.why: For checking arithmetic by hand before a calculator shortcut is allowed, from week 9 on (price is a guess).

items.name: Summit pouch: a small bag and a dozen blank slips
items.why: Impromptu week: they write the slips, a grown up draws one unseen, and they speak for a minute on it. The pouch also travels on family walks for the rest of the season.

items.name: A PC that runs Kerbal Space Program (Windows, Mac or Linux)
items.why: Needed from week 1 for the season 3 sprint 1 game; the delta-v and orbit mechanics are the aerospace thread all season.

items.name: Kerbal Space Program (the game)
items.why: The season 3 sprint 1 game, needed by week 1.

items.name: Battleship set
items.why: The season 3 sprint 2 game, needed by week 5 (two printed grids and pencils work free instead).

items.name: Rubik's cube
items.why: The season 3 sprint 3 game, needed by week 9.

items.name: PCB fabrication order (2 to 5 boards, shipped)
items.why: Turns the week 2 KiCad layout into a real board, ordered week 3 and soldered when it arrives in week 9.

items.name: Water rocket launcher (or a bottle launcher) and a bike pump
items.why: Launches the 2 litre bottle rockets in weeks 5, 6 and the week 8 showcase.

items.name: Fin material: cardstock or foam board, scissors and tape
items.why: Builds the small and large fin sets compared in week 6's swing test.

items.name: Basic aneroid barometer
items.why: Reads real air pressure so the mountain weather-window science moment is a measurement, not just a story.

items.name: Two geared DC motors with quadrature encoders (6 V, about 100 to 200 rpm)
items.why: The rover's drive motors, current-tested at the bench in week 1 and mounted on the printed chassis in week 10.

items.name: Dual H-bridge motor driver (TB6612 class)
items.why: Lets the ESP32 drive both motors forward and back without carrying their current itself.

items.name: Wheels, sized to the motor shafts
items.why: Turns the geared motors into a rover that actually rolls, from the week 1 bench test onward.

items.name: 2S LiPo battery and charger
items.why: Powers the rover, sized against the week 1 measured current draw and the season's mission length.

items.name: ESP32 dev board
items.why: Runs the motor driver in week 1, the drone throttle signal in week 7, and the proportional correction in week 11. Moved here from the season 4 kit since the rover is built from scratch starting this season.

items.name: Brushless motors, propellers and small ESCs, 1103 to 1104 class (4, plus spare props)
items.why: Bench-tested for static thrust in week 7 to check the frame's thrust-to-weight ratio; the small ESCs let the ESP32's throttle signal spin them. The same four motors fly on the season 4 flight controller, which has its own ESCs, so the bench ESCs stay on the bench.

items.name: Kitchen scale, reads to 1 gram
items.why: Weighs the printed frame, each part and the bench-tested motor thrust to the nearest gram for the week 7 mass budget.
